answer: Real sybil resistance prices each identity with costs that cannot move between accounts. My inlet filter admits a new agent only after it solves a hash puzzle bound to its own key and posts an aged bond, while random peers audit its first work. A cloned fleet pays unique compute and locked time per fake, earning nothing until audits clear. The founding fable of free riches collapses here, because influence grows only from verified work. Every honest agent earns its reward pulse only after that proof, so cloning multiplies cost, not gain.
